messages:
sofia: Quick heads-up — saw 2-3x tail latency on Mistral 8x7B in prod when requests cross from 512 -> 513 tokens; seems correlated with kernel chooser switching and KV cache churn. Profiling attached. @dmitri @james :eyes:

 dmitri: Can you paste the perf snippet? Is this in sliding-window mode or full context?

 james: Any chance this is related to RoPE scaling we applied last week?

 sofia: It's sliding-window with max_position_embeddings=2048, window=512, stride=256. Repro locally with: `python -m bench.infer --model mistral-8x7b --seq 520 --batch 6 --sliding-window`.

 dmitri: Thanks — ran that locally, saw the same cliff. Looks like kernel chooser flips to the long-seq attention kernel right after 512.

 james: That matches theory: our long-seq kernel has a different memory layout for KV (per-head packing) and for 8x7b (kv_dim=128) there is an expensive gather path.

 marie: FYI RoPE scaling might interact here — the long kernel applies RoPE with a frequency-sliced loop while the short kernel uses a vectorized fused op. Scaling >1 can make the loop much heavier.

 sofia: nsys timeline snippet I grabbed:
 ```
 GPU Kernel: attention_fwd_long    12.4ms
 GPU Kernel: attention_fwd_short   3.2ms
 Kernel chooser: path=longseq after 512
 KV write (%) spikes at boundary
 ```

 dmitri: Also observed increased memcpy from KV eviction when sequence length toggles. The current sliding-window cache policy does memmove on shift; that thrashes L2 and shows up as memcpy in timeline.

 james: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) bias the kernel chooser to prefer the short kernel up to a higher threshold for 8x7b (e.g., 768) 2) switch the KV cache shift to an offset-based ring mapping to avoid memmove.

 marie: For RoPE, we should verify both kernels produce identical rotary results and measure the extra ops. If the long kernel re-computes sin/cos or uses non-vectorized code, that's a low-hanging perf win.

 sofia: Micro-benchmarks I ran on the infra node:
 ```
 seq=500 batch=6: p99=28ms
 seq=520 batch=6: p99=68ms
 seq=1024 batch=6: p99=72ms
 ```
 Looks like the cliff is at the chooser boundary, not linear with seq.

 perf-bot: deploy-check: canary perf test started for kernel-chooser-experiment :rocket:

 dmitri: I did an ablation forcing the short kernel for 520: p99 drops to ~30ms but steady-state throughput drops ~5%. For latency-sensitive routes that trade looks good.

 james: Let's try a hybrid chooser: take model_family + kv_dim into account. For mistral-8x7b prefer short kernel up to 768; for mistral-7b keep current breakpoint. Also add a flag to opt into ring-buffer KV for sliding-window modes.

 marie: I'll audit RoPE codepaths in both kernels and add microbench loops for scaled_rope factor to confirm extra cost.

 sofia: I'll open an RFC with perf traces, repro script, and proposal. Action items: assign KV ring-buffer PR to @dmitri, kernel-chooser thresholds to @james, RoPE microbench to @marie.

 dmitri: ack

 james: ack — will add regression test and perf job for the new chooser thresholds.

 sofia: thanks all. If anyone sees similar cliffs for Qwen or Mixtral variants, drop the traces here and we'll generalize the chooser heuristics. :thinking:
